body.statement: For independent sample splits of sizes \(n_1,n_2\), \[\inf_{G_0,\Sigma_0}\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\ge1-\alpha_1,\qquad \inf_{G_0,\Sigma_0}\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\in\{\operatorname{SCC}(G):G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\}\ge1-\alpha_1.\] For every true \((\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in\Theta_{G_0}\) and every \(u,v\in V\) with \(u\ne v\), \(\Pr\{(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\}\ge1-\alpha_2\) and \(\Pr\{\tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})\in\mathcal I_{u\to v}\}\ge1-\alpha\).
body.justification: The set-valued construction keeps structural and parameter uncertainty visible instead of conditioning on one learned graph.
body.gap: Wang, Kolar, and Drton and Strieder et al. give DAG uncertainty procedures; SCC recovery alone does not identify coefficients, so this result unions over graphs and parameter roots.
body.consumer: A signaling analyst can report a feedback-module confidence set and a conservative equilibrium-intervention effect set without treating the selected graph as known.
